newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent trims losses in choppy trade, rescales $.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent trims losses in choppy trade, rescales $.

text.p: IPE Brent futures extended its selloff to new session lows and then rebounded to back above $23 a barrel in choppy trading ahead of the NYMEX products expiry at the close.
Profit taking to this week's gains and weakness in NYMEX heating oil knocked prices lower, then Brent recovered after holding above its session low from Thursday, traders said.

At 1657 GMT, March Brent was off three cents at $23.15 a barrel after dropping to as low as $22.81. Feb gas oil traded $1.25 lower at $210.75 a tonne after falling to $206.50, just above a gap at $205.50.

Jeff Potter, managing director at Dublin-based Univest Ireland, said volume has been lighter the past few sessions which has increased the volatility. He also said there was likely some profit taking in the Feb/March gas oil spread after heavy buying had widened that spread.
"Overall it's still looking pretty negative," he said, adding the rally earlier this week was primarily a correction to the losses the previous two weeks.
Despite the choppy trade, March Brent has held within its session range from Thursday, a sign of consolidation.
